name: Sacchi's zonal pressing
scopeNote: Idea of the compact zonal 4-4-2 with collective pressing, short lines (max ~25 m between defence and front line) and a high offside trap, as practised by Sacchi's Milan 1987-91 (manager id arrigo-sacchi, team id milan-1988-91). Sources call it zonal marking / zonal pressing / 'pressing' (Coaches' Voice: 'a zonal defence'); Sacchi stressed it was 'controlling space', not running. Popular label 'pure Total Football copy' or 'defensive' is partial: Coaches' Voice and Holding Midfield cite Total Football as influence, FIFA says he opposed man-marking and the sweeper. Sacchi's Italy (1991-96) used the same 4-4-2 but is outside this period. Most sources are retrospective (2012-2023); eventDate is a season range where no match date was given. Period uses the manager file's Milan spell (1987-07-01 to 1991-06-30). No source read gives a dated 1987-91 contemporary report. The Italian-language searches (Sky Sport Italia) returned unreadable pages.
openQuestions: Was Milan the first Italian zonal team? Holding Midfield says first, but notes Vinicio's Napoli and Liedholm's Roma had experimented; Mannari says players were used to a slow zonal marking before Sacchi.
Sacchi's own zonal system is called both 'zonal marking' and 'zonal pressing'; 'mixed zone' (zona mista) belongs to Trapattoni and is not Sacchi's.
The old offside rule: Coaches' Voice says any attacker in advance of the defensive line was offside; FIFA says level with the last defender was offside. Differing descriptions of the same law.
Sacchi's link to the Gegenpressing lineage (Frank, Klopp) was seen only in a search summary, not read.

sources.title: Arrigo Sacchi and his Italian revolution - Forza Italian Football
sources.evidence: Sacchi liked his teams to fundamentally use a zonal-marking system. Setting up in a simple 4-4-2 formation (see right), he made sure that the defence and midfield were never 25 metres apart. This meant that the opposition would struggle to penetrate the team through the middle, and almost always be forced to go out wide.

sources.title: Pressing-Meisterwerk: Die Taktik hinter Arrigo Sacchis Erfolg - Fussballcoach
sources.evidence: Die Grundlage seiner Taktik war eine raumorientierte Verteidigung. Die Spieler sollten gemeinsam über das Spielfeld verschieben und die Abstände zueinander gleichmäßig halten.
